title: 2025 AMC 12A Problem 24
statement: A circle of radius \(r\) is surrounded by \(12\) circles of radius \(1,\) externally tangent to the central circle and sequentially tangent to each other, as shown. Then \(r\) can be written as \(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are integers. What is \(a + b + c?\)

solutions.text:
The centers of the \(12\) outer circles lie on a circle of radius \(r + 1,\) forming a regular \(12\)-gon. Adjacent centers are \(2\) apart (both circles have radius \(1\)), and the central angle between them is \(30^\circ.\)

Thus \(2(r + 1)\sin 15^\circ = 2,\) so \(r + 1 = \dfrac{1}{\sin 15^\circ}.\) Since \(\sin 15^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4},\) \[r + 1 = \frac{4}{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}.\]

Then \(r = \sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2} - 1,\) so \(a + b + c = 6 + 2 - 1 = 7.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The \(12\) outer centers form a regular \(12\)-gon of circumradius \(r + 1,\) with adjacent centers \(2\) apart
